normalization.constant_channel_rule: q99-q01 <= 1e-8 maps to zero; inverse maps to q01; mask stays true
normalization.gripper_rule: continuous channels 6 and 13; same quantile transform as the twelve arm channels
normalization.source: train episodes only; every real target row joint_action/vector[1:] used once each; the initial drive-target row has no preceding observation and is excluded; no horizon repetitions and no padding rows
normalization.target_rows: joint_action/vector[1:] per train episode; rows used once each

protocol.action_space: ALOHA14 absolute drive-target joints and continuous normalized grippers
protocol.bank_reset: before every group; all queries within a group belong to one episode
protocol.image_decoder: RMBench decode_image_bit; legacy-unmarked/XPL-RGB1 auto-detection; output RGB
protocol.label_alignment: observation[t] -> joint_action/vector[t+1:t+1+H]; each label is the next recorded absolute drive target, not measured qpos and not a certified next-issued command
protocol.padding: repeat the final real target row; valid_mask false for every padded horizon timestep; the final recorded RGB frame has no target row and is never supervised
protocol.query_schedule: 0, execute_prefix, 2*execute_prefix, ... <= episode_length - 2 (strictly below episode_length - 1, so every query has at least one following target row); consecutive disjoint groups
semantic_risks: Native labels are captured absolute drive targets, not measured qpos, and are not a certified next-issued command. With target_offset=1 a target row is the next recorded absolute drive target; closed-loop validation is still required.
Historical HDF5 files lack per-frame collector commit provenance, so the exact command issued between two recorded frames cannot be reconstructed from the file alone.
New XPolicyLab state/action HDF5 shifts targets by one frame and reorders packed channels; it is intentionally not accepted as this native format.
